the N-terminal domain of Ad E1A 24R represses MYCN in human cancer cell lines by targeting p300 and TRAPP, and that repression of MYCN is associated with inhibition by E1A of acetylation at H3K18/H4K16 in the MYCN promoter.
the E1A 143R oncoprotein targets both p300 and the TRRAP histone acetylases to repress MYC transcription and expression in human cancer cells.
the E1A N-domain represses HER2 and MYC expression in human cancer cells and that repression of MY C occurs by inhibition of histone acetylation and RNA Pol II binding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the E1A 80 amino acid transcriptional repression domain (E1A R) inhibits gene transcription.
the regulation of gene expression by viral oncoproteins and how these viral proteins may be used as a therapeutic tool to treat human cancers.
understanding the cellular pathways regulating transcription and expression of oncogenes.

the Ad E1A oncoprotein can target two important pathways of histone modification to inhibit transcription of proto-oncogene HER2 and MYC in human breast cancer cell lines.
